Subject: Post-demo: model fit + regression concerns (BlueWave)

Hi Samantha / Tom —

Thanks again for the time earlier — appreciated the detailed walkthrough of BlueWave's triage flow. Per our conversation, here's a concise recap, where we landed on model fit, and the immediate items we think are important given your note about a recent quality dip after a model version update.

Recap / hypothesis:
- BlueWave needs stable, high-precision clinical intent classification at short prompts (~60–120 tokens).
- You reported a ~6% drop in classification accuracy after an internal model bump last week — appears correlated with the model family change (v3.2 -> v3.2-quant).
- Primary concern is user-facing false-negatives on priority labels; secondary is cost throughput.

What we recommended on the call:
1) Short-term mitigation: pin the serving model to v3.1-stable for the affected route while we investigate diffs.
2) Technical triage: run our diff/eval harness on your production prompt set (we'll run locally in Private VPC or send CIDs if you prefer).
3) Benchmarks & prompt sets: share the benchmark results link + prompt set (attached: prompt_set_v2.jsonl).
4) Next steps / timeline: Redwood will deliver a regression diff report (by EOD tomorrow) and a rollback plan if regression confirmed.

Attachments included for your reference: prompt_set_v2.jsonl (sample prompts + labels), and a template kanban_next_steps.csv for tracking.

Immediate ask from you: can you confirm who owns the change that pushed v3.2-quant? If you prefer, we can coordinate rollback and then run the evaluation mode to compare delta.

I'll put Monica on the thread for the technical deep-dive. Thanks —

— Rishi

- The change was deployed by our ML infra team as part of a company-wide quantization rollout; I'll loop them in separately but Tom is owner for the production route.
- We absolutely want to pin to v3.1-stable if Redwood can apply that in the next 24 hours; the false-negatives are hitting clinical triage SLAs.

On Thu, Apr 2, 2026 at 10:03 AM Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@bluewavehealth.com> wrote:
> Can you confirm whether pinning will affect throughput targets we discussed (we need to keep 200 req/s peak).

Hi Samantha — quick technical note from my side:
- Pinning to v3.1-stable: expected 3–5% throughput reduction vs v3.2-quant (quantization gives a throughput boost) but we preserve accuracy. On your 200 req/s target, v3.1-stable on the Dedicated config we discussed should maintain ~190–195 req/s steady-state; we can add modest burst capacity to meet 200 req/s peaks without changing latency SLOs.
- I've run a targeted sample diff (attached: model_diff_report.pdf) comparing v3.2-quant vs v3.1-stable on your provided prompt set (1000 labeled examples). High-level: overall accuracy -6.2% (v3.2-quant worse), false-negative rate on 'high-priority' label increased from 4.1% -> 9.8%.
- Root causes: quantization-induced calibration shift on short sequences; some tokenization edge-cases in the custom clinical vocab.

Proposed immediate actions:
1) We recommend pinning the production route to v3.1-stable tonight. Redwood can push a config change (requires your infra ok) — takes ~20–30 minutes with safe rollback.
2) While pinned, we'll run a full eval harness across the 10k prompt set and produce a detailed diff and per-label token-level heatmap (deliverable: full diff report + remediation suggestions).
3) Medium term: we suggest a re-calibration pass for v3.2-quant with a small prompt-tuning step and tokenization patch for clinical tokens.

Attachments: model_diff_report.pdf (summary + charts), prompt_set_v2.jsonl.

I'll coordinate with Dylan to schedule the config pin and the evaluation run; Dylan, can you propose two windows (tonight and tomorrow morning) where we can do the pin with BlueWave infra?

— Monica

Thanks Monica — the numbers are concerning. Two quick asks from our side:
1) We need a guaranteed rollback window in case pinning creates unexpected regressions in other labels; can you provide a play-by-play rollback plan and an expected RTO?
2) If you recommend prompt-tuning for v3.2-quant, what is the expected lift and how long until we can test? We have a compliance freeze next week and would prefer not to touch production during that window.

Goal: keep the production user impact to zero while we validate fixes. Do you have a one-page risk matrix we can share with our risk/compliance team?

— Tom

Tom / Samantha — quick summary and concrete next steps so we all have the same runbook: 

Actions (owners + ETA):
- Pin production route to v3.1-stable (owner: Redwood infra / Dylan; ETA: tonight 20:00 PT) — expected downtime: none; config update ~20–30 min; safe rollback included.
- Full eval harness run across 10k prompts (owner: Monica; ETA: EOD tomorrow) — deliverable: full diff report + per-label heatmaps (will upload to drive and link).
- Rollback playbook & RTO: Dylan will submit a step-by-step rollback doc; expected RTO < 30 minutes. (owner: Dylan Brooks; ETA: 2 hours).
- Prompt-tuning experiment for v3.2-quant (owner: Redwood research; ETA: 2 weeks for initial candidate, 4 weeks for full validation) — note: we will not touch production during BlueWave's compliance freeze unless you explicitly approve.
- Risk matrix one-pager for your compliance team (owner: Rishi; ETA: tomorrow morning) — will include exposure, mitigations, and monitoring hooks.

I'll open a HubSpot task with the action items and share the Drive folder link (see related_links). Monica will post the model_diff_report.pdf and prompt_set_v2.jsonl to the shared folder once the full run completes.

If that plan looks good, Samantha please confirm we have permission to schedule tonight's pin at 20:00 PT and confirm the on-call for rollback.

Thanks again — we'll keep this tight.

— Rishi
